records.source: כֹּֽה־אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ שַׁ֜עַר הֶחָצֵ֤ר הַפְּנִימִית֙ הַפֹּנֶ֣ה קָדִ֔ים יִהְיֶ֣ה סָג֔וּר שֵׁ֖שֶׁת יְמֵ֣י הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂ֑ה וּבְי֤וֹם הַשַּׁבָּת֙ יִפָּתֵ֔חַ וּבְי֥וֹם הַחֹ֖דֶשׁ יִפָּתֵֽחַ׃
records.gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: [The] gate of the court the inner that faces east will be shut [the] six days of work, and on the day of the Sabbath it will be opened, and on the day of the new moon it will be opened.
pieces: the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: The gate of the inner court that faces east is to stay shut during the six working days, but it is to be opened on the Sabbath and at the new moon.

L.1: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: The gate of the inner court that faces east is to be shut on the six working days, but on the Sabbath day it is to be opened, and on the day of the new moon it is to be opened.

R.1: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: The east gate of the inner courtyard must stay shut on the six working days. But it must be opened on the Sabbath day and on the first day of each month.

decisions.choice: thus says the Lord GOD: the LORD's speech of 44:5 continues
decisions.reason: There is no new narrative frame; the LORD is still speaking to Ezekiel, as in 45:9 and 45:18. His speech runs to 46:18.

decisions.choice: the gate of the inner court that faces east: not the shut outer east gate
decisions.reason: The outer east gate stays shut for ever (44:1-2). This is the east gate of the inner court, which faces the altar and the temple. It is opened only on holy days.

decisions.choice: the first day of each month (R)
decisions.reason: As 45:17 at Readable.

records.heading: Offerings for Sabbaths and new moons

records.source: וּבָ֣א הַנָּשִׂ֡יא דֶּרֶךְ֩ אוּלָ֨ם הַשַּׁ֜עַר מִח֗וּץ וְעָמַד֙ עַל־מְזוּזַ֣ת הַשַּׁ֔עַר וְעָשׂ֣וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֗ים אֶת־עֽוֹלָתוֹ֙ וְאֶת־שְׁלָמָ֔יו וְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲוָ֛ה עַל־מִפְתַּ֥ן הַשַּׁ֖עַר וְיָצָ֑א וְהַשַּׁ֥עַר לֹֽא־יִסָּגֵ֖ר עַד־הָעָֽרֶב׃
records.gloss: And the prince will enter [by] [the] way of [the] porch of the gate from outside and stand by [the] doorpost of the gate, and the priests will offer his burnt offering and his peace offerings, and he will bow down at [the] threshold of the gate and go out; and the gate will not be shut until the evening.
pieces: The prince is to come in from outside through the porch of the gate and stand by the doorpost of the gate. The priests are to offer his burnt offering and his peace offerings, and he is to bow down in worship at the threshold of the gate and then go out. But the gate is not to be shut until evening.

L.2: And the prince will enter by way of the porch of the gate from outside and stand by the doorpost of the gate; and the priests will offer his burnt offering and his peace offerings, and he will bow down at the threshold of the gate, and [then] go out; but the gate will not be shut until evening.

R.2: The ruler must come in from the outer courtyard through the porch of the gate and stand beside the doorpost. The priests will offer his burnt offering and his peace offerings. He must bow down and worship at the doorway of the gate. Then he must leave. But the gate must not be shut until evening.

decisions.choice: the prince stands at the doorpost: he sees the offerings but does not enter the inner court
decisions.reason: The prince comes into the gate building from the outer court, through its porch, which in the inner gates faces outward (40:31), and stands at the inner end, where he can see the altar. Only the priests go into the inner court to offer (44:15-16).

decisions.choice: he shall bow down: he worships
decisions.reason: The verb is the regular word for bowing in worship. The prince leads the people in worship but does so as a worshiper (verse 3).

decisions.choice: prince (L, B); ruler (R)
decisions.reason: As in 44:3.

records.source: וְהִשְׁתַּחֲו֣וּ עַם־הָאָ֗רֶץ פֶּ֚תַח הַשַּׁ֣עַר הַה֔וּא בַּשַּׁבָּת֖וֹת וּבֶחֳדָשִׁ֑ים לִפְנֵ֖י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And [the] people of the land will bow down [at] [the] entrance of that gate on the Sabbaths and on the new moons before Yahweh.
pieces: The people of the land are to bow down in worship before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at the entrance of that gate on the Sabbaths and the new moons.

L.3: And the people of the land will bow down at the entrance of that gate before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the Sabbaths and on the new moons.

R.3: On the Sabbath days and on the first day of each month, the people of the land must bow down and worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at the entrance to that gate.

decisions.choice: the people of the land: the ordinary people of Israel
decisions.reason: The phrase means the people at large, as distinct from the prince and the priests (7:27; 45:16, 22).

decisions.choice: at the entrance of that gate: outside it, in the outer court
decisions.reason: The people stay in the outer court, before the open gate, and worship from there.

records.source: וְהָ֣עֹלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־יַקְרִ֥ב הַנָּשִׂ֖יא לַֽיהוָ֑ה בְּי֣וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֗ת שִׁשָּׁ֧ה כְבָשִׂ֛ים תְּמִימִ֖ם וְאַ֥יִל תָּמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And the burnt offering which the prince will offer to Yahweh on the day of the Sabbath: six lambs unblemished and a ram unblemished.
pieces: The burnt offering that the prince offers to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the Sabbath day is to be six lambs without defect and a ram without defect,

L.4: And the burnt offering that the prince will offer to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the Sabbath day [will be] six lambs without blemish and a ram without blemish,

R.4: On the Sabbath day the ruler must offer to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} a burnt offering of six lambs and one ram. None of them may have anything wrong with them.

decisions.choice: six lambs and a ram: more than the law's Sabbath offering
decisions.reason: Numbers 28:9-10 required two lambs on the Sabbath, besides the daily offering.

records.source: וּמִנְחָה֙ אֵיפָ֣ה לָאַ֔יִל וְלַכְּבָשִׂ֥ים מִנְחָ֖ה מַתַּ֣ת יָד֑וֹ וְשֶׁ֖מֶן הִ֥ין לָאֵיפָֽה׃
records.gloss: And a grain offering, an ephah for the ram, and for the lambs a grain offering [as] the gift of his hand, and oil, a hin to the ephah.
pieces: with a grain offering of {{units:about 6 gallons|an ephah}} for the ram, and for the lambs as much as he chooses to give, with {{units:about a gallon|a hin}} of oil for each ephah.

L.5: and the grain offering [will be] an ephah for the ram, and for the lambs a grain offering as much as he is able to give, and a hin of oil for each ephah.

R.5: With them he must give a grain offering of {{units:about 6 gallons|an ephah}} of flour for the ram, and for the lambs as much flour as he wishes. He must also give {{units:about a gallon|a hin}} of olive oil for each ephah of flour.

decisions.choice: the gift of his hand: as much as he wants to give
decisions.reason: The phrase means a gift left to the giver, as much as he is able or chooses to give (Deuteronomy 16:17).

decisions.choice: {{units:about 6 gallons|an ephah}}; {{units:about a gallon|a hin}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 45:24.

records.source: וּבְי֣וֹם הַחֹ֔דֶשׁ פַּ֥ר בֶּן־בָּקָ֖ר תְּמִימִ֑ם וְשֵׁ֧שֶׁת כְּבָשִׂ֛ם וָאַ֖יִל תְּמִימִ֥ם יִהְיֽוּ׃
records.gloss: And on [the] day of the new moon: a bull, a young one of [the] herd, unblemished, and six lambs and a ram; unblemished they will be.
pieces: On the day of the new moon he is to offer a young bull without defect, and six lambs and a ram, all without defect.

L.6: And on the day of the new moon [he will offer] a young bull without blemish, and six lambs and a ram; they will be without blemish.

R.6: On the first day of each month he must offer a young bull, six lambs and a ram. None of them may have anything wrong with them.

decisions.choice: the new moon offering: smaller than the law's
decisions.reason: Numbers 28:11 required two bulls, a ram and seven lambs at each new moon. Ezekiel's lists are not the same as the law's.

records.source: וְאֵיפָ֨ה לַפָּ֜ר וְאֵיפָ֤ה לָאַ֨יִל֙ יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה מִנְחָ֔ה וְלַ֨כְּבָשִׂ֔ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּשִּׂ֖יג יָד֑וֹ וְשֶׁ֖מֶן הִ֥ין לָאֵיפָֽה׃
records.gloss: And an ephah for the bull and an ephah for the ram he will provide [as] grain offering, and for the lambs as his hand reaches, and oil, a hin to the ephah.
pieces: He is to provide a grain offering of {{units:about 6 gallons|an ephah}} with the bull and {{units:about 6 gallons|an ephah}} with the ram, and with the lambs as much as he can, together with {{units:about a gallon|a hin}} of oil for each ephah.

L.7: And an ephah for the bull and an ephah for the ram he will provide [as] a grain offering, and for the lambs as much as he can afford, and a hin of oil for each ephah.

R.7: With them he must give a grain offering of {{units:about 6 gallons|an ephah}} of flour for the bull and {{units:about 6 gallons|an ephah}} for the ram. For the lambs he may give as much as he can. He must also give {{units:about a gallon|a hin}} of olive oil for each ephah of flour.

decisions.choice: as his hand reaches: as much as he can afford
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of what a person can afford (Leviticus 5:7; 14:21-22).

records.source: וּבְב֖וֹא הַנָּשִׂ֑יא דֶּ֣רֶךְ אוּלָ֤ם הַשַּׁ֨עַר֙ יָב֔וֹא וּבְדַרְכּ֖וֹ יֵצֵֽא׃
records.gloss: And when the prince comes in, by [the] way of [the] porch of the gate he will come in, and by its way he will go out.
pieces: When the prince enters, he is to come in through the porch of the gate and go out the same way.

L.8: And when the prince enters, he will come in by way of the porch of the gate, and he will go out the same way.

R.8: When the ruler comes in, he must come in through the porch of the gate, and he must leave the same way.

records.source: וּבְב֨וֹא עַם־הָאָ֜רֶץ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָה֮ בַּמּֽוֹעֲדִים֒ הַבָּ֡א דֶּרֶךְ־שַׁ֨עַר צָפ֜וֹן לְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֗ת יֵצֵא֙ דֶּרֶךְ־שַׁ֣עַר נֶ֔גֶב וְהַבָּא֙ דֶּרֶךְ־שַׁ֣עַר נֶ֔גֶב יֵצֵ֖א דֶּרֶךְ־שַׁ֣עַר צָפ֑וֹנָה לֹ֣א יָשׁ֗וּב דֶּ֤רֶךְ הַשַּׁ֨עַר֙ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֣א ב֔וֹ כִּ֥י נִכְח֖וֹ יֵצֵֽא׃
records.gloss: And when [the] people of the land come before Yahweh at the appointed feasts, the one who comes in [by] [the] way of [the] gate of [the] north to bow down will go out [by] [the] way of [the] gate of [the] south, and the one who comes in [by] [the] way of [the] gate of [the] south will go out [by] [the] way of [the] gate northward; he will not return [by] the way of the gate by which he came in, but straight ahead he will go out.
pieces: At the appointed festivals, when the people of the land come before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, those who come in by the north gate to worship are to go out by the south gate, and those who come in by the south gate are to go out by the north gate. No one is to go back through the gate by which they came in; each is to go straight out the opposite side.

L.9: But when the people of the land come in before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at the appointed times, whoever comes in by way of the north gate to worship will go out by way of the south gate, and whoever comes in by way of the south gate will go out by way of the north gate. No one will return by way of the gate by which he came in, but each will go out straight ahead.

R.9: When the people of the land come to worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at the special festivals, those who come in through the north gate must leave through the south gate. Those who come in through the south gate must leave through the north gate. No one may go back out through the gate they came in by. Everyone must go straight across and out the opposite gate.

decisions.choice: in by one gate and out by the other: an orderly flow of crowds
decisions.reason: At the great festivals large crowds came to the temple. The rule keeps them moving in one direction. The east gate of the outer court is shut (44:2), so the people use the north and south gates.

decisions.choice: he will go out: the written text and the reading tradition differ
decisions.reason: The written text reads the verb as plural ("they will go out") and the reading tradition as singular. The sense is the same.

records.source: וְֽהַנָּשִׂ֑יא בְּתוֹכָ֤ם בְּבוֹאָם֙ יָב֔וֹא וּבְצֵאתָ֖ם יֵצֵֽאוּ׃
records.gloss: And the prince, in their midst, when they come in, he will come in, and when they go out, they will go out.
pieces: The prince is to be among them, coming in when they come in and going out when they go out.

L.10: And the prince will be among them: when they come in, he will come in, and when they go out, they will go out [together].

R.10: The ruler must be among the people. He must come in with them and go out with them.

decisions.choice: the prince among them: he worships with the people
decisions.reason: At the festivals the prince does not stand apart but enters and leaves with the people. The text pictures a ruler who shares the people's worship.

decisions.choice: they will go out: the plural joins the prince and the people
decisions.reason: The last verb is plural, so the prince and the people go out together.

records.source: וּבַחַגִּ֣ים וּבַמּוֹעֲדִ֗ים תִּהְיֶ֤ה הַמִּנְחָה֙ אֵיפָ֤ה לַפָּר֙ וְאֵיפָ֣ה לָאַ֔יִל וְלַכְּבָשִׂ֖ים מַתַּ֣ת יָד֑וֹ וְשֶׁ֖מֶן הִ֥ין לָאֵיפָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And at the festivals and at the appointed feasts the grain offering will be an ephah for the bull and an ephah for the ram, and for the lambs the gift of his hand, and oil, a hin to the ephah.
pieces: At the festivals and the appointed feasts the grain offering is to be {{units:about 6 gallons|an ephah}} with a bull and {{units:about 6 gallons|an ephah}} with a ram, and with the lambs as much as he chooses to give, together with {{units:about a gallon|a hin}} of oil for each ephah.

L.11: And at the festivals and the appointed feasts the grain offering will be an ephah per bull and an ephah per ram, and for the lambs as much as he is able to give, and a hin of oil for each ephah.

R.11: At the festivals and special feasts, the grain offering must be {{units:about 6 gallons|an ephah}} of flour for each bull and {{units:about 6 gallons|an ephah}} for each ram. For the lambs he may give as much as he wishes. He must also give {{units:about a gallon|a hin}} of olive oil for each ephah of flour.

decisions.choice: festivals and appointed feasts: the great pilgrim feasts and the other holy days
decisions.reason: The first word names the three pilgrim festivals; the second, all the set times of worship (45:17).

records.source: וְכִֽי־יַעֲשֶׂה֩ הַנָּשִׂ֨יא נְדָבָ֜ה עוֹלָ֣ה אֽוֹ־שְׁלָמִים֮ נְדָבָ֣ה לַֽיהוָה֒ וּפָ֣תַֽח ל֗וֹ אֶתהַשַּׁ֨עַר֙ הַפֹּנֶ֣ה קָדִ֔ים וְעָשָׂ֤ה אֶת־עֹֽלָתוֹ֙ וְאֶת־שְׁלָמָ֔יו כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲשֶׂ֖ה בְּי֣וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֑ת וְיָצָ֛א וְסָגַ֥ר אֶת־הַשַּׁ֖עַר אַחֲרֵ֥י צֵאתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And when the prince provides a freewill offering, a burnt offering or peace offerings, a freewill offering to Yahweh, then he will open for him the gate that faces east, and he will provide his burnt offering and his peace offerings as he provides on the day of the Sabbath; and he will go out, and he will shut the gate after his going out.
pieces: When the prince provides a freewill offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, whether a burnt offering or peace offerings, the gate facing east is to be opened for him, and he is to present his burnt offering or his peace offerings just as on the Sabbath day. When he goes out, the gate is to be shut behind him.

L.12: And when the prince makes a freewill offering, a burnt offering or peace offerings, [as] a voluntary gift to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the gate facing east will be opened for him, and he will offer his burnt offering and his peace offerings as he offers on the Sabbath day; and he will go out, and the gate will be shut after he has gone out.

R.12: Sometimes the ruler may choose to bring a burnt offering or a peace offering as a gift to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Then the east gate must be opened for him. He must offer his burnt offering or his peace offerings in the same way as on the Sabbath day. After that he must leave, and the gate must be shut after him.

decisions.choice: a freewill offering: an offering given by choice, not by command
decisions.reason: The law allowed freewill offerings at any time, as burnt offerings or peace offerings (Leviticus 22:18-23; Numbers 15:3).

decisions.choice: he will open ... he will shut: someone opens and shuts the gate
decisions.reason: The verbs have an unnamed subject, probably the gatekeeper.

decisions.choice: the gate is to be opened ... shut (B, R)
decisions.reason: The unnamed subject (m2) is rendered with a passive.

records.heading: Freewill offerings and the daily offering

records.source: וְכֶ֨בֶשׂ בֶּן־שְׁנָת֜וֹ תָּמִ֗ים תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה עוֹלָ֛ה לַיּ֖וֹם לַֽיהֹוָ֑ה בַּבֹּ֥קֶר בַּבֹּ֖קֶר תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And a lamb, a son of its year, unblemished, you will provide [as] a burnt offering daily to Yahweh; morning by morning you will provide it.
pieces: Every day you are to provide a lamb a year old without defect as a burnt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; you are to provide it morning after morning.

L.13: And you will provide a lamb a year old without blemish as a burnt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} daily; morning by morning you will provide it.

R.13: Every morning you must offer a lamb one year old as a burnt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It must have nothing wrong with it.

decisions.choice: the daily burnt offering: in the morning only
decisions.reason: The law required a lamb every morning and every evening (Exodus 29:38-42; Numbers 28:3-8). Ezekiel names only the morning offering.

decisions.choice: you will provide: the address changes from the prince to "you"
decisions.reason: The verbs change to "you" (singular). The Septuagint reads "he will provide", meaning the prince. The Hebrew may address the prophet or the people as a whole.

records.source: וּמִנְחָה֩ תַעֲשֶׂ֨ה עָלָ֜יו בַּבֹּ֤קֶר בַּבֹּ֨קֶר֙ שִׁשִּׁ֣ית הָֽאֵיפָ֔ה וְשֶׁ֛מֶן שְׁלִישִׁ֥ית הַהִ֖ין לָרֹ֣ס אֶת־הַסֹּ֑לֶת מִנְחָה֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה חֻקּ֥וֹת עוֹלָ֖ם תָּמִֽיד׃
records.gloss: And a grain offering you will provide with it morning by morning, a sixth of the ephah, and oil, a third of the hin, to moisten the fine flour, a grain offering to Yahweh; statutes forever, continually.
pieces: With it you are to provide a grain offering every morning: {{units:about a gallon|a sixth of an ephah}} of flour and {{units:about 1 1/4 quarts|a third of a hin}} of oil to moisten the fine flour. This grain offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is a lasting statute, to be kept continually.

L.14: And you will provide a grain offering with it morning by morning, a sixth of the ephah, and oil, a third of the hin, to moisten the fine flour, [as] a grain offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, a perpetual statute, continually.

R.14: With it you must give a grain offering every morning. Give {{units:about a gallon|a sixth of an ephah}} of fine flour and {{units:about 1 1/4 quarts|a third of a hin}} of olive oil to moisten it. This is the grain offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. This law must be obeyed for all time.

decisions.choice: statutes forever, continually: a rule that lasts for all time
decisions.reason: The phrase "a statute forever" is used of the lasting rules of worship in Leviticus (Leviticus 3:17; 6:11). "Continually" is the word for the regular daily offering (verse 15).

decisions.choice: {{units:about a gallon|a sixth of an ephah}}; {{units:about 1 1/4 quarts|a third of a hin}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: On the ephah of about 6 gallons (45:11); a third of a hin as published (Numbers 28:14).

records.source: יַעֲשׂ֨וּ אֶת־הַכֶּ֧בֶשׂ וְאֶת־הַמִּנְחָ֛ה וְאֶת־הַשֶּׁ֖מֶן בַּבֹּ֣קֶר בַּבֹּ֑קֶר עוֹלַ֖ת תָּמִֽיד׃פ
records.gloss: And they will provide the lamb and the grain offering and the oil morning by morning, a burnt offering continually.
pieces: So the lamb, the grain offering and the oil are to be provided every morning as a regular burnt offering.

L.15: Thus they will provide the lamb, the grain offering and the oil, morning by morning, as a regular burnt offering.

R.15: So the lamb, the grain offering and the olive oil must be offered every morning as the daily burnt offering.

decisions.choice: they will provide: the written text and the reading tradition differ
decisions.reason: The written text reads "provide" without a clear subject; the reading tradition has "they will provide". The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: a burnt offering continually: the regular daily offering
decisions.reason: The phrase is the name of the daily burnt offering (Numbers 28:6; Daniel 8:11).

records.source: כֹּה־אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה כִּֽי־יִתֵּ֨ן הַנָּשִׂ֤יא מַתָּנָה֙ לְאִ֣ישׁ מִבָּנָ֔יו נַחֲלָת֥וֹ הִ֖יא לְבָנָ֣יו תִּֽהְיֶ֑ה אֲחֻזָּתָ֥ם הִ֖יא בְּנַחֲלָֽה׃
records.gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: If the prince gives a gift to any of his sons, it is his inheritance; it will belong to his sons; it is their holding by inheritance.
pieces: the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: If the prince makes a gift of land to any of his sons, it will become part of the son's inheritance. It will belong to his sons as their property by inheritance.

L.16: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: If the prince gives a gift to any of his sons [out of his inheritance], it will belong to his sons; it is their holding by inheritance.

R.16: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: If the ruler gives some of his land as a gift to one of his sons, it will belong to that son and his descendants. It will be their property to pass on.

decisions.choice: to any of his sons, his inheritance: the gift becomes the son's inheritance
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is brief: "to a man of his sons, his inheritance it is". It means the land given becomes the son's own inheritance. The Septuagint reads "from his inheritance".

decisions.choice: the prince's land stays in his family
decisions.reason: Verses 16-18 keep the prince's land, and the people's, from being lost. Land given to his sons stays with them; land given to his servants returns (verse 17); and he may not take the people's land (verse 18).

decisions.choice: a gift of land (B); some of his land (R)
decisions.reason: The gift is land, as verses 17-18 show.

records.heading: The prince's land

records.source: וְכִֽי־יִתֵּ֨ן מַתָּנָ֜ה מִנַּחֲלָת֗וֹ לְאַחַד֙ מֵֽעֲבָדָ֔יו וְהָ֤יְתָה לּוֹ֙ עַד־שְׁנַ֣ת הַדְּר֔וֹר וְשָׁבַ֖ת לַנָּשִׂ֑יא אַ֚ךְ נַחֲלָת֔וֹ בָּנָ֖יו לָהֶ֥ם תִּהְיֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And if he gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his servants, it will be his until [the] year of liberty, and it will return to the prince; only his inheritance, his sons', it will be theirs.
pieces: But if he makes one of his servants a gift from his inheritance, the servant may keep it until the year of release. Then it will go back to the prince. His inheritance belongs to his sons alone.

L.17: But if he gives from his inheritance a gift to one of his servants, it will be his until the year of liberty; then it will revert to the prince. Only his sons may keep his inheritance.

R.17: But if he gives some of his land to one of his officials, it will belong to that official only until the year of freedom. Then it must go back to the ruler. Only his sons may keep his land.

decisions.choice: the year of liberty: the jubilee year
decisions.reason: Every fiftieth year land returned to the family that first owned it and Hebrew slaves were freed (Leviticus 25:10-13). The word "liberty" is the one used there, and in Jeremiah 34:8 and Isaiah 61:1.

decisions.choice: his servants: the prince's officials
decisions.reason: The word *'eved* here means a servant of the ruler, a royal official, as often (2 Kings 22:12).

decisions.choice: servants (L, B); officials (R)
decisions.reason: As the Isaiah table gives for court officials (*'eved*) at Readable.

decisions.choice: the year of liberty (L); the year of release (B); the year of freedom (R)
decisions.reason: Each level says the jubilee year in its own words (m1).

records.source: וְלֹא־יִקַּ֨ח הַנָּשִׂ֜יא מִנַּחֲלַ֣ת הָעָ֗ם לְהֽוֹנֹתָם֙ מֵאֲחֻזָּתָ֔ם מֵאֲחֻזָּת֖וֹ יַנְחִ֣ל אֶת־בָּנָ֑יו לְמַ֨עַן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־יָפֻ֣צוּ עַמִּ֔י אִ֖ישׁ מֵאֲחֻזָּתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And the prince will not take from the inheritance of the people, to oppress them, from their holding; from his own holding he will give an inheritance to his sons, so that my people will not be scattered, anyone from his holding.
pieces: The prince must not take any of the people's inheritance, driving them off their property. He is to give his sons their inheritance out of what he himself owns, so that none of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people will be scattered from their property."

L.18: And the prince will not take from the people's inheritance, thrusting them out of their holding. He will give his sons their inheritance out of his own holding, so that none of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people will be scattered from his holding."

R.18: The ruler must not take any of the people's land and force them off it. He must give his sons land only from his own property. Then none of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people will be driven from their land."

decisions.choice: the prince shall not take the people's inheritance: against the abuse of royal power
decisions.reason: The verse forbids what Ahab did to Naboth (1 Kings 21) and what Samuel warned a king would do (1 Samuel 8:14). It answers 45:8-9.

decisions.choice: the end of the LORD's speech
decisions.reason: The speech that began in 44:5 ends here. In verse 19 the guide leads Ezekiel on through the temple.

decisions.choice: holding (L); property (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 45:5.

decisions.choice: closing quotation mark (all levels)
decisions.reason: The quotation opened in 44:5 closes here.

records.source: וַיְבִיאֵ֣נִי בַמָּבוֹא֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־כֶּ֣תֶף הַשַּׁעַר֒ אֶל־הַלִּשְׁכ֤וֹת הַקֹּ֨דֶשׁ֙ אֶל־הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים הַפֹּנ֖וֹת צָפ֑וֹנָה וְהִנֵּה־שָׁ֣ם מָק֔וֹם בַּיַּרְכָתַ֖יִם יָֽמָּה׃ס
records.gloss: And he brought me in [by] the entrance which [was] at [the] side of the gate to the rooms of holiness for the priests, which faced northward; and look, there [was] a place at the far end westward.
pieces: Then the man led me through the entrance beside the gate to the priests' holy rooms facing north, and there I saw a place at the far western end.

L.19: Then he brought me through the entrance that [was] at the side of the gate to the holy chambers of the priests, which faced north; and look, there [was] a place at the far end on the west.

R.19: Then the man took me through the doorway beside the gate into the holy rooms for the priests. The rooms faced north. At the far west end of them I saw a special place.

decisions.choice: he brought me: the guide of chapters 40-42
decisions.reason: The narrative of the tour resumes. The speaker of verse 20 is the guide, as in 42:13.

decisions.choice: the holy rooms for the priests: the rooms of 42:1-14
decisions.reason: These are the rooms on the north side of the temple, where the priests ate the most holy offerings (42:13).

decisions.choice: the man (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 44:1, so that the guide is not taken for the LORD.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י זֶ֣ה הַמָּק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֤ר יְבַשְּׁלוּ־שָׁם֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים אֶת־הָאָשָׁ֖ם וְאֶת־הַחַטָּ֑את אֲשֶׁ֤ר יֹאפוּ֙ אֶת־הַמִּנְחָ֔ה לְבִלְתִּ֥י הוֹצִ֛יא אֶל־הֶחָצֵ֥ר הַחִֽיצוֹנָ֖ה לְקַדֵּ֥שׁ אֶת־הָעָֽם׃
records.gloss: And he said to me, This [is] the place where the priests will boil the guilt offering and the sin offering, where they will bake the grain offering, so as not to bring [them] out to the court the outer, to make holy the people.
pieces: He said to me, "This is the place where the priests are to boil the guilt offering and the sin offering and bake the grain offering, so that they do not bring them out into the outer court and pass on holiness to the people."

L.20: And he said to me, "This [is] the place where the priests will boil the guilt offering and the sin offering, [and] where they will bake the grain offering, so as not to bring [them] out into the outer court and make the people holy."

R.20: He said to me, "This is where the priests must boil the meat of the guilt offerings and the sin offerings. They must also bake the grain offerings here. Then they will not have to carry these holy offerings into the outer courtyard, where their holiness might pass to the people."

decisions.choice: to make the people holy: holiness passing to the people
decisions.reason: As in 44:19, the most holy offerings must not come into contact with the people, lest they be made holy and come under the rules for holy things.

decisions.choice: pass on holiness to the people (B); where their holiness might pass to the people (R)
decisions.reason: As in 44:19.

records.heading: The temple kitchens

records.source: וַיּוֹצִיאֵ֗נִי אֶל־הֶֽחָצֵר֙ הַחִ֣יצֹנָ֔ה וַיַּ֣עֲבִירֵ֔נִי אֶל־אַרְבַּ֖עַת מִקְצוֹעֵ֣י הֶחָצֵ֑ר וְהִנֵּ֤ה חָצֵר֙ בְּמִקְצֹ֣עַ הֶחָצֵ֔ר חָצֵ֖ר בְּמִקְצֹ֥עַ הֶחָצֵֽר׃
records.gloss: And he brought me out to the court the outer, and he led me past to [the] four corners of the court; and look, a court in [the] corner of the court, a court in [the] corner of the court.
pieces: Then he brought me out into the outer court and took me around to each of its four corners. In each corner of the court there was another small court.

L.21: Then he brought me out into the outer court and led me past the four corners of the court; and look, in each corner of the court [there was] a court.

R.21: Then he took me out to the outer courtyard. He led me around to its four corners. In each corner there was a smaller courtyard.

decisions.choice: a court in the corner of the court, a court in the corner of the court: a court in each corner
decisions.reason: The repetition is the Hebrew way of saying "in every corner".

records.source: בְּאַרְבַּ֜עַת מִקְצֹע֤וֹת הֶֽחָצֵר֙ חֲצֵר֣וֹת קְטֻר֔וֹת אַרְבָּעִ֣ים אֹ֔רֶךְ וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֖ים רֹ֑חַב מִדָּ֣ה אַחַ֔ת לְאַרְבַּעְתָּ֖ם מְׄהֻׄקְׄצָׄעֽׄוֹׄתׄ׃
records.gloss: In [the] four corners of the court [were] courts enclosed, forty length and thirty breadth; one measure for the four of them, set in corners.
pieces: In the four corners of the court were enclosed courts, {{units:about 70 feet|forty cubits}} long and {{units:about 52 1/2 feet|thirty cubits}} wide. All four corner courts were the same size.

L.22: In the four corners of the court [were] enclosed courts, forty [cubits] long and thirty wide; the four in the corners [had] one measure.

R.22: In each of the four corners of the outer courtyard there was a closed courtyard. Each one was {{units:about 70 feet|forty cubits}} long and {{units:about 52 1/2 feet|thirty cubits}} wide. All four were the same size.

decisions.choice: enclosed: a rare word, perhaps "small" or "smoky"
decisions.reason: The word is found only here. It is usually taken as "enclosed" or "walled off". Some ancient versions read "small", and some connect it with a word for smoke, from the cooking done there.

decisions.choice: set in corners: a word marked in the Hebrew
decisions.reason: The last word is marked with special dots in the Hebrew manuscripts, a sign the scribes doubted it. It repeats the sense of "in the corners".

records.source: וְט֨וּר סָבִ֥יב בָּהֶ֛ם סָבִ֖יב לְאַרְבַּעְתָּ֑ם וּמְבַשְּׁל֣וֹת עָשׂ֔וּי מִתַּ֥חַת הַטִּיר֖וֹת סָבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: And a row [of stones] [was] all around in them, around the four of them, and boiling places [were] made under the rows all around.
pieces: Around the inside of each of the four courts ran a ledge of stone, with places for cooking built under the ledges all around.

L.23: And [there was] a row [of stone] all around inside them, around the four of them, with places for boiling made under the rows all around.

R.23: A stone ledge ran around the inside of each of the four courtyards. Under the ledges there were fireplaces for cooking.

decisions.choice: a row: a course or ledge of stone
decisions.reason: The word means a row, as of stones in a wall (1 Kings 6:36). Here it is probably a ledge of stone with hearths beneath it.

records.source: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑י אֵ֚לֶּה בֵּ֣ית הַֽמְבַשְּׁלִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֧ר יְבַשְּׁלוּ־שָׁ֛ם מְשָׁרְתֵ֥י הַבַּ֖יִת אֶת־זֶ֥בַח הָעָֽם׃
records.gloss: And he said to me, These [are] [the] house of those who boil, where the ministers of the house will boil [the] sacrifice of the people.
pieces: He said to me, "These are the kitchens where those who serve in the temple are to boil the people's sacrifices."

L.24: And he said to me, "These [are] the kitchens where the ministers of the house will boil the sacrifices of the people."

R.24: He said to me, "These are the kitchens where the temple servants will cook the meat of the sacrifices the people bring."

decisions.choice: the sacrifices of the people: the peace offerings, eaten by the worshipers
decisions.reason: The worshipers ate most of the meat of their peace offerings as a feast before the LORD (Leviticus 7:15-18; Deuteronomy 12:7). The Levites, "the ministers of the house" (44:11, 14), cooked it in the outer court, apart from the priests' kitchens.

decisions.choice: kitchens (all levels)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "house of those who boil" means kitchens; every level says so.
